summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded C++ and Linux experience across STM32, NVIDIA Jetson, and Raspberry Pi platforms. Built and deployed a multi-device robotic arm system on Linux with Git-managed code, ROS2 and Python tooling, and debugged 11 hardware and software integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability. Skilled in bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, and UART/I2C/SPI communication.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Debugged and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place arm as a distributed Linux system: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller linked over a unified WebSocket fabric.

Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a Linux systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root user/group isolation, environment-file config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device registration.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ and drove five servos with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed a Cortex-M4 temperature monitor in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS2 driver, validated against MoveIt and RViz models in ROS2 Humble; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.
